full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Karim J: These seven Criminal Appeals (Criminal Appeal Nos. 895 of 1990, 932 of 1990, 925 of 1990, 990 of 1990, 958 of 1990, 923 of 1990 and 1020 of 1990) are directed against the judgment and order dated 10-9-90 passed by the learned Divisional Special Judge, Chittagong, in Special Case No. 2 of 1989 convicting appellants Hamiduzzaman Chowdhury, General Manager, Md. Fazlul Karim and Muhammad Kamruzzaman, Deputy General Managers of Agrani Bank, Serajul Islam, previous Manager, Ansarul  Hoque, incumbent Manager of Khatunganj Branch, Nirmal Mollik, 2nd officer, Abdus Sukur, Officer in-Charge Cash and C D and Mainuddin Chowdhury, Cashier of the said branch and Bibhuti Bhusan Talukder having CD A/C No 4702 in the said branch and sentencing them under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act H of 1947 to different terms of imprisonment, fine and confiscation of property. This judgment will dispose of all the seven appeals as they arise out of the same judgment and order. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that appellant Bibhuti Bhushan Talukder maintained one current account being CD. A/C. No. 4702 in the name of his firm, M/s SB Traders, at Khatunganj Branch of Agrani Bank. At the time of the alleged occurrence on 8-7-86 the credit balance in the said account was Taka 1530.40. Accused Bibhuti Bhusan Talukder in collusion with some officials of the said branch presented a bearer cheque bearing No. 1077261 dated 26-6-86 for Taka 4,00,00,000.00 for payment in cash. On 8-7-86 the accused persons, officials of the said branch, in collusion with one another encashed the cheque and made payment of taka four crore although the total credit balance in the account was only Taka 1530.40. Accused appellant Bibhuti Bhushan misappropriated the amount with the abetment of the officials of the branch. The matter was reported to the Deputy Director, Bureau of Anti-Corruption over telephone at 2-30 P M on 9-7-86 and the Deputy Director sent PW 1 Md. Arif Siddiquee, Inspector, Bureau of Anti-Corruption to the office of the General Manager, Chittagong. On reaching the office PW 1 saw accused Abdus Sukur, officer-in charge of Cash and CD sitting in front of the General Manager and at that time appellant Ansarul Haque, Manager of Khatunganj Branch, handed over a petition of complaint under his signature (Ext. 1) to PW 1. The formal First Information Report (Ext. 12) was lodged on 16-7-86 by PW 1 alleging misappropriation of an amount of taka four crore with the abetment of the officials of the bank, that accused Abdus Sukur posted the cheque in the ledger and did the work of cancellation with his initials, that the Manager, namely, Ansarul Haque, kept himself away from supervision of the ledger, cancellation of the cheque and cash payment on that day, that accused Nirmal Mallick, 2nd officer having custody of one key of the cash vault, also did not do the usual supervision of the ledger posting or cancellation of the cheque or payment of cash and that accused Mainuddin Chowdhury, Cashier having the custody of one key of the cash vault, illegally paid an amount of taka four crore though the credit balance of the said account No. 4702 was Taka 1,530/40 and without the signature of the Manager on the cheque, which was necessary for making payment of a big amount. On completion of the investigation a charge sheet was submitted by the Bureau of Anti-Corruption against the officials of the bank and Bibhuti Bhusan Talukder. 

 3. At the time of the trial the prosecution examined 11 witnesses as against none by the defence. It is also the allegation against the incumbent Manager, Ansarul Haque, and the former Manager, appellant Serajul Islam, that they allowed cash to remain in the bank in excess of the safe limit of Taka 20,00,000.00 and that usually an amount of more than taka one crore used to remain in the bank in violation of the circular of the head office. The allegation against appellant M Kamruzzaman and appellant Md. Fazlul Karim, two Deputy General Managers, is that they did not regularly visit the Branch and supervise its functioning and failed to enforce the regular transmission of the excess amount to the feeding branch, namely, Laldighi branch, The allegation against appellant Hamiduzzaman Chowdhury is that being the General Manager of the Bank, he failed to exercise proper supervision over the branch under his control, particularly the Khatunganj branch, which was noted as being one of the core branches of Agrani Bank. 

 4. The defence of accused appellant Ansarul Haque is that he was not directly concerned with the cash transaction of the branch, inasmuch as he was primarily concerned with the development work and supervision over the officials of the branch. His further defence is that the cheque in question (Ext. 3) was posted in the ledger by accused Abdus Sukur, officer in-charge of Cash and CD who also did the work of supervision and cancellation of the cheque under his initials and that the cheque in question was never brought to his notice by the Second officer, CD in charge Abdus Sukur or the Cashier and he had no knowledge about the cheque or payment in connection thereof. The defence of appellant Mainuddin Chowdhury, Cashier of the branch, is that he had no knowledge of the receipt of the cheque, ledger posting or cancellation of the cheque, which was done by Abdus Sukur alone in his hand and under his initials and though as the cashier he was custodian of one key of the cash vault, he had no occasion to make payment of the cheque. The defence of appellant Serajul Islam, former Manager, is that he was not in charge of the branch at the time of the occurrence and had no occasion to do anything on the transaction about the said cheque. The defence of the two Deputy General Managers, namely, M Kamruzzaman and Md. Fazlul Karim, is that their responsibility was limited to supervision over the branches within their jurisdiction without any thing to do with the cash transaction of any particular branch and that they always directed the managers under their control for lifting of the excess cash to the feeding branch. The defence of the General Manager, namely, Hamiduzzaman Chowdhury, is that he had no concern with the work of the cash section of any particular branch and there were 313 branches in his jurisdiction and that it was not humanly possible on the part of the General Manager to know what was happening precisely in a particular branch. 

 5. Having considered the evidence, oral and documentary, the learned Special Judge found appellant Ansarul Haque, Manager of the Branch, guilty of the offence under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and convicted him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six years, to pay a fine of Taka 50 (fifty) lac, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year and six months without any separate sentence under section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. The trial Court found second officer Nirmal Mallick and Abdus Sukur, officer in-charge of Cash and CD (both being tried in absentia) guilty of the offence under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code and convicted and sentenced each of them to suffer imprisonment for life. The court further imposed on Nirmal Mallick a fine of taka one crore, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7 years and confiscated all his properties. The court also imposed on Abdus Sukur a fine of Taka four crore, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7 years and confiscated all his properties. The court also convicted Mainuddin Chowdhury, Cashier under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code and also under section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 convicting him to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Taka 25 (twenty-five) lac, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7 years. The court found appellant Bibhuti Bhusan Talukder guilty under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code and also under section 420 of the Penal Code and sentenced him to suffer imprisonment for life without any separate sentence under section 420 of the Penal Code, and to pay fine of taka four crore, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7 years and confiscated all his properties acquired after 1983. The Court also convicted Serajul Islam, the previous manager of the branch, under section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and sentenced thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months with a fine of taka one lac, in default, to suffer RI for one month. The Court convicted Md. Kamruzzaman, Deputy General Manager, under section 5(2) of Act H of 1947 and sentenced him thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year and to pay a fine of taka five lac, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three months. The court also convicted Mr. Fazlul Karim, Deputy General Manager, under section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and sentenced him thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months and to pay a fine of taka one lac, in default, to suffer RI for one month. Lastly, the court convicted Hamiduzzaman Chowdhury, General Manager, under section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and sentenced him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year and to pay a fine of taka five lac in default, to suffer RI for 3 months. 

 7. The prosecution case comes, in short, from the evidence of PW 1 Md. Arif Siddique, Inspector of Bureau of Anti-Corruption, and he is informant of the case. On 9-7-86 at about 2-30 PM a telephone call was received by Deputy Director, Bureau of Anti-Corruption about misappropriation of money in Khatunganj Chittagong Branch. PW 1 states that at once he along with another Inspector, under direction of the Deputy Director, came to the office of appellant Hamiduzzaman Chowdhury, who was the General Manager, Eastern Circle, Chittagong. On arrival at the branch PW 1 found absconding accused Abdus Sukur, officer-in-charge of CD and Cash Department of the Branch, sitting in front of the General Manager and at that time appellant Ansarul Haque, Manager of the Branch, presented to PW 1 a petition of complaint (Ext. 1) about the misappropriation of money in his Branch, PW 1 seized a number of documents including a cheque bearing No. 1077261 dated 26-6-86 in respect of CD A/C No. 4702 owned by Bibhuti Bushan Talukder in the name of his firm, M/s SB Traders. PW 1 further seized paying Cashiers Book (Ext. 7) page 54 of which shows payment of taka four crore on the basis of this cheque. PW 1 further seized the ledger (Ext. 4) about posting of four crore taka for the cheque against A/C No. 4702 though the cash balance on that day (8-7-86) was only taka 1530/40. He also seized receiving cashiers book. (Ext. 8). In his evidence PW 1 states that absconding accused Abdus Sukur posted the cheque in the ledger, cancelled the cheque and did the work of supervision about the said cheque and that the Manager (Ansarul Haque) kept himself away from cancellation of the cheque and supervision of the ledger. Cashier Mainuddin Chowdhury paid taka four crore on the basis of the said cheque with the full knowledge that the cheque did not bear initials of the Manager as per rules for payment of big amounts. Nirmal Mallick, second officer of the bank, being one of the joint custodians of cash of the bank, did not supervise the ledger and vouchers and the payment of four crore taka on a fictitious token bearing number 65 was made from the said account although a paltry amount was in deposit in the said account. PW 1 further states that at the end of the day on 8-7-86, the closing balance of Taka 3,52,803/15 was jointly signed by cashier Mainuddin Chowdhury and CD in-charge and Cash officer, Abdus Sukur. 

 8. The prosecution case gyrates round a self drawn cheque (Ext. 3) bearing the date 26-6-86 of Agrani Bank Current Account No. 4702. The CD ledger (Ext. 4) and the account opening form (Ext. 10) shows that CD Account was opened in Khatunganj Branch by appellant Bibhuti Bushan Talukder in the name of his firm, SB Traders, on 5-7-83. The ledger Ext. 4 shows Taka 1,530/40 as the balance against CA No. 4702 when the cheque (Ext. 3) bearing the date 26-6-86 was presented and also encashed for taka four crore on 8-7-86. Though the cheque bears the date 26-6-86, it bears token No. 65 dated 8-7-86. This shows that the concerned persons were waiting to encash it after accumulation of sufficient cash in the Branch. PW 1 Md. Arif Siddique, Inspector of Bureau of Anti Corruption on preliminary inquiry lodged the formal First Information Report on 16-7-86 (Ext. 12). He has proved page 54 of the paying cashiers book (Ext. 7) serial 62 of which mentions payment of taka four crore against CA No. 4702 on 8-7-86 on the basis of cheque No. 1077261. PW 1 states that this payment of taka four crore was made though the ledger (Ext. 4) shows only a balance of taka 1530/40 against CA No. 4702 held by appellant Bibhuti Bushan Talukder on the basis of this unauthorised and concealed overdraft, without following the rules of the bank regarding cancellation of cheque, ledger supervision and payment, causing loss to the bank to the tune of Taka. 3,99,98,469.60. In this connection PW 1 states in his examination in-chief that absconding accused Abdus Sukur having a key of the cash vault in his custody (being the officer in charge of cash and CD) in his hand and under his initials posted the cheque in the ledger, supervised and cancelled the cheque and also put a fictitious token number 65 on the back of the cheque. In his evidence PW 1 further states that the incumbent Manager, namely appellant Ansarul Haque, kept himself away from the cheque cancellation and ledger supervision and appellant Mainuddin Chowdhury Cashier, paid Taka 4 (four) crore though the cheque was not properly supervised, cancelled and initialled by the Manager for payment of such a huge amount and that Nirmal Mallick, second officer of the bank and one of the joint custodians of the bank cash and also holding one of the keys of the cash iron safe (cash vault), did not supervise cash payment, ledger posting and supervision of vouchers at the end of the day leaving it to the subordinate to remove such a huge amount from the bank. 

 9. Mr. Khademul Islam Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the incumbent Manager Ansarul Haque, in Criminal Appeal No. 932 of 1990, submits that as per evidence the payment of Taka 4 crore appears to have been made on the basis of the cheque in question by absconding accused Abdus Sukur, officer-in-charge of CD and Cash Department, and the said accused posted the cheque in the ledger, issued a token bearing No. 65, supervised and cancelled the cheque under his own initials and further, that the making of payment was the responsibility of the cashier namely, Mainuddin Chowdhury, who did not at any stage bring the cheque to the notice of the Manager. Mr. Khademul Islam Chowdhury accordingly, submits that Manager Ansarul Haque had no occasion to know about the cheque in question, lack of sufficient amount in CD account No. 4702 and that all this was managed by cash and CD In-charge, Abdus Sukur, in collusion with Bibhuti Bushan Talukder the holder of the said account. Mr. Chowdhury further submits that Ansarul Haque during his incumbency as the Manager directed Abdus Sukur, Cash officer and CD in-charge, to send the excess amount over the safe limit to the feeding branch, but the latter did not comply with his order and further that the lifting of the excess amount was the responsibility of the feeding branch (Laldighi Branch). 

 11. PW 6 Meenu Das was an officer of Khatunganj Branch of Agrani Bank from May, 1983 to 13th July, 1986. She produced the attendance register of Khatunganj Branch for the period from November, 1984 to 19th July, 1986. This register shows that after the departure of appellant Serajul Islam, appellant Ansarul Haque became Manager of the Branch and continued till 11-7-86 (from 28-2-86 to 11-7-86). The Attendance Register further shows that absconding accused Nirmal Mallick was second officer, absconding accused Abdus Sukur was officer in charge of cash and CD Department, appellant Mainuddin Chowdhury was the cashier at the relevant period including the date of occurrence on 8-7-86. In her cross-examination PW 6 states that Mainuddin Chowdhury and Abdus Sukur sat side by side in the office and that Mainuddin Chowdhury was the head cashier with three Assistant Cashiers, namely Shamsul Haque, Shajahan and Krishna Gopal. PW 7 Tofail Ahmed who took over charge of Manager of Khatunganj Branch after 19-7-86 from Manager Nesar Ahmed, has produced the key register (Ext. 17) showing that there were three keys for the large iron safe (cash safe) of the cash vault of the Branch. PW 7 states that key No. 50115/2 (Master key) was with him while he was the manager and that it is the responsibility of the Branch Manager to keep the master key with him. The 2nd key bearing No. 50115/A1 was with the second officer, absconding accused Nirmal Mallick, from 13-3-86 to 9-7-86 and that third key bearing No. 50115/B1 was with cashier, Mainuddin Chowdhury, from-372-85 to 9-7-86. PW 7 further states that from 30-12-83 to 9-7-86 the master key was with absconding accused Abdus Sukur. The evidence of PW 7 further makes it clear that safety of the cash of the Branch is the responsibility of the Branch Manager, the Cashier and the CD in charge and that the protection of the cash of the Branch is the clear responsibility of those who have the custody of the keys of the iron safe. In cross examination for appellant Mainuddin Chowdhury, PW 7 states that the Master key and the 2nd key bearing No. 50115/A1 being with the superior officers, it was not possible to open the cash vault with only one key, which was with the cashier. The cross examination further shows that there are two counters of cash, one is receiving counter and the other is paying counter, and that cash officer and CD in charge is primarily responsible in matters of cash and that the cash department works under his supervision. 

 13. In this cross examination for Mainuddin Chowdhury P W 7 Tofael Ahmed, who worked as Manager Khatunganj Branch immediately after the occurrence, states that during his incumbency there was only one cashier in Khatunganj Branch. There is therefore, no room for doubt that on 8-7-86 Mainuddin Chowdhury was the receiving and paying Cashier with three other Assistant Cashiers to assist him. In his statement under section 342 of the Criminal Procedure Code, appellant Mainuddin has disowned the signature (Ext. 9/A) dated 8-7-86 in the Receiving Cashiers Book. We have already observed that there is absolutely no reason to disbelieve the evidence of PW 2 and PW 6 responsible officers of the bank, that the signature (Ext. 9/A) in the Receiving Cashiers Book on 8-7-86 was that of appellant Mainuddin Chowhury. In this connection we have carefully examined the hand-writing under signature of Mainuddin Chowdhury for several days appearing in the Paying Cashiers Book and those appearing in the Receiving Cashiers Book for the month of July, 1986, and similarity of these writings and signatures leads us to the conclusion that appellant Mainuddin Chowdhury worked as Receiving and Paying Cashier at the relevant time particularly on 8-7-86. 

 18. The method of cash payment is incorporated in Agrani Bank Service Rules as per SRO 311-L/81 of Ministry of Finance (Banking and Investment Division) vide. Ext. 'W' published in Bangladesh Gazette on 12th September 1981. It is specifically mentioned in this instruction that on receipt of a cheque, the cashier's duty is to see whether it is duly posted with marking by the ledger keeper and cancelled with the initials of the cancellation officer and in case of payment of a big amount whether it was cancelled with the initials of two officers including the Manager. In the instant case, the payment of a huge amount of bank money was made without following the usual banking practice and instruction. In his evidence PW 7 Tofail Ahmed, who was manager of Khatunganj Branch immediately after the occurrence, states that it is the responsibility of the Branch Manager CD in-charge and the Cashier to protect the cash of the bank. He further states that the holders of the keys of the large iron safe (cash safe) of the cash vault have the responsibility to protect the cash of the bank. It is in the evidence of this witness supported by the key register (Ext. 17) that Nirmal Mallick, second officer, was the custodian of one of the keys of the iron safe and as second officer he had the responsibility of supervision of ledger posting and payment of cash. The evidence and circumstances of the case clearly show that absconding accused Abdus Sukur and Nirmal Mallik and Cashier Mainuddin Chowdhury by corrupt or illegal means and by abusing their position as public servants obtained illegal payment of taka four crore to appellant Bibhuti Bushan Talukder through an unauthorised and concealed overdraft. The learned Special Judge rightly convicted these three accused persons guilty of the offence under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act,1947 (Act II of 1947). 

 19. Mr. Khademul Islam Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing for appellant Ansarul Haque in Criminal Appeal No. 932 of 1990, has submitted that in the light of the evidence on record, particularly of PW 1, PW 6 and the investigation officer (PW 11), the prosecution has no case against Ansarul Haque, who happened to be Manager on the day of the occurrence. In First Information Report lodged on 16-7-86 (Ext. 12). PW 1 Arif Siddiquee mentions that Abdus Sukur, officer in-charge of CD in connivance with the officials of Khatunganj Branch, received the cheque all by himself, posted the same in the ledger and cancelled it under his initials. 

 20. The evidence of P W 6 Meenu Das, in the same tenor, states that Abdus Sukur passed the cheque after posting it in the ledger. In his cross examination PW 1 states, it does not appear from the documents seized by me that the cheque (Ext. 3) was placed before Manager Ansarul Haque. The ledger keeper, CD in charge or the cashier did not bring the disputed cheque to the notice of the Manager. In his cross-examination PW 4 Ibrahim Khalid, General Manager of the Bank, states: 

 There is no doubt that it was not possible for the Manager to know of the cash payment unless the cheque was placed before him for cancellation or instruction. In the instant case concerned officials including the ledger keeper, cash officer cum CD in charge or the Cashier did not bring the cheque to the notice of the manager and they fraudulently did so with the object of arranging an unauthorised, cancelled overdraft in violation of the practice of the bank to insist on cheque cancellation under initials of the Manager in case of big payments. 

 21. Mr. Syed Abu Kowser, learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the State, has submitted that in the instant case the Manager did nothing to supervise the ledger and other Accounts Books of the Bank and to arrange for lifting of the excess cash over safe limit of taka twenty lac. In this connection Mr. Abu Kowser has drawn our attention to Ext 'A', a circular, issued by the General Manager directing the Branch Managers to arrange the lifting of the excess cash to the feeding branch. The cross examination of PW 4 Ibrahim Khaled, General Manager of the Bank, shows that usually the cash in hand in Khatungang Branch lay between taka two crore and three crore. There is enough evidence to show that the cash in hand in the Branch usually exceeded taka one crore though the safe limit fixed by the authorities was only taka 20 lac. In his cross examination PW 4 says that there was excess cash in every branch of Agrani Bank at that time which is partially true. But there is a difference between a minor amount and a major amount. 

 22. Mr. Khademul Islam Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing for appellant Ansarul Haque, has submitted that the Manager directed Abdus Sukur, CD in charge and Cash Officer, not to keep any excess cash in hand and in this connection he has drawn our attention to (Ext. '13') dated 21-5-86 directing Abdus Sukur to arrange transmission of the excess cash to the feeding branch. The evidence of PW 2 Ferdousuzzaman, Sr. Principal Officer, Laldighi Branch, runs as follows: 

 "Laldighi Branch is the feeding Branch for Khatunganj. The excess cash of Khatunganj is to be sent to Laldighi Branch. If cash is required it is to be taken from Laldighi through requisition. The security arrangement for cash lifting is for Laldighi Branch or Khatunganj Branch to arrange. There is no vault in the Zonal Office (headed by the Deputy General Manager). There are two vehicles in the Laldighi Branch for carrying cash. 

 There is no doubt that it has become the practice of Khatunganj Branch for a very long time, even during the period when appellant Serajul Islam was the Manager before appellant Ansarul Haque, to keep a huge amount of taka one crore or two crore in the Branch. There is no doubt that this has been in violation of the circular against keeping any excess amount in the Branch. 

 23. Mr. Khademul Islam Chowdhury has argued that the onus is on the prosecution to prove mens rea or criminal intent and without this there can be no conviction against the accused. We have considered this aspect very carefully. Mere violation of rules and instructions cannot be ground for finding the accused guilty of the offence under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5 (2) of Act II of 1947. In such a case the prosecution is bound to prove mens rea or criminal intent which is lacking in this case. In the facts and circumstances of the case, it is open to the Department (Agrani Bank) to probe the acts of commission and omission, if any, committed by appellant Ansarul Haque during his incumbency as the Manager of Khatunganj Branch. 

 25. There is no dispute that CD No. 4702 in the name of M/s SB Traders owned by appellant Bibhuti Bhushan Talukder was opened in Khatunganj Branch on 5-7-83 and that only a sum of Taka 1530/40 was the cash balance in this account on 8-7-86. In his evidence PW 1 Md. Arif Siddique, Inspector of Bureau of Anti Corruption, states that on receipt of a phone call at 2-30 PM on 9-7-86 he was directed by the Deputy Director Anti Corruption, to go to the office of the General Manager, namely, appellant Hamiduzzaman Chowdhury, where on arrival he found absconding accused Abdus Sukur, officer in-charge of CD and Cash Department, sitting in front of the General Manager and at that moment the incumbent Manager namely, Ansarul Haque, presented to him a petition of complaint about misappropriation of Taka 3,99,98,469/60 against CD account No. 4702 held by appellant Bibhuti Bushan Talukder on the basis of a cheque bearing number 1077261 dated 26-6-86. In his evidence PW 1 states that Abdus Sukur in his hand posted the cheque in the ledger, supervised and cancelled the cheque under his initials after putting a fictitious token number on the back of the cheque. In cross examination PW 1 states that Bibhuti Bushan had three other accounts with condition similar to the instant account in the same Branch. It appears from the cross examination of PW 6 Meenu Das that though the date was noted in token number, the time of presentation was not noted en the back of the cheque and further that denomination of notes was also not noted on the back of the cheque, which is usually done by the bank. The cross-examination of PW 6 further shows marks of over-writing against serial numbers 63 to 69 in the Paying Cashiers Book (Ext. 7). 

 29. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud has submitted that false deposit in Khatunganj Branch had been going on for a long time. In this connection he has invited our attention to cross-examination of PW 7 Tofael Ahmed (Manager of the Bank) wherein he states that account No. 4445 in Khatunganj Branch is in the same name of Swapon Kumar Ghose. A/C 4137 is in the name of Haridas Ghose and A/C 5457 is in the name of Eastern Timber Industries and the audit report mentions false deposits in these accounts for which Kotwali Police Station Case No. 8(6)88 dated 8-5-88 was filed against the employees of the bank. In cross examination PW 11 (Investigating Officer) has admitted that PW 1 filed an First Information Report marked x (20) under sections 409/420/471/109 read with section 5 (2) of Act 11/1947 against Swapon Kumar Chose, convicted accused Abdus Sukur, convicted accused Nirmal Mallick and Appellant Mainuddin Chowdhury and some other officers of the Bank for misappropriation of the bank money from 23-12-85 to 8-7-86. The First Information Report alleges temporary misappropriation of Taka 6,20,00,000 through fraudulent paperwork in the ledger and other account books of the bank. Mr. Mahmud submits that this First Information Report dated 8-6-86 shows that Haridas Chose and his son, Swapon Kumar Chose, in collusion with the officials of Khatunganj Branch through a false deposit of taka 1,80,00,000 in their accounts Nos. 4137, 5457 and 4445 managed to withdraw on 8-7-86 (the same day) a sum of Taka 1,60,00,000. 

 34. Now about the appeals preferred by the two Deputy General Managers, being Criminal Appeal No. 895 of 1990 by the previous Deputy Manager, Md. Fazlul Karim, who was the Deputy General Manager upto 10-10-85 i.e. long before the date of occurrence on 8-7-86 and Criminal Appeal No. 958 of 1990 filed by Mr. Kamruzzaman, Deputy General Manager at the time of occurrence. As in the case of the Manager, Ansarul Haque in Criminal Appeal No. 932 of 1990, we do not find materials indicating the presence of mens rea or criminal intent by these two Deputy General Managers, who were in no way connected with the daily affairs or business transactions of the branch and were merely exercising supervisory jurisdiction over a large number of branches. Accordingly, we find that these two appellants, Md. Fazlul Karim and M Kamruzzaman are not guilty of the offence under section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and the order of conviction and sentence passed against them should be set aside. Similarly, the learned Assistant Attorney-General has failed to satisfy us as to what offence Hamiduzzaman Chowdhury, the General Manager, has committed inasmuch as it is on record that he had in his jurisdiction 13 regions and 313 branches. It would be better if the persons in charge of management of the financial institutions of the country knew the line where to stop raising the finger. We accordingly find appellant Hamiduzzaman Chowdhury not guilty of the offence under section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and the order of conviction and sentence passed against him should be set aside. 

 38. The department concerned may prove the acts of commission and omission against the incumbent Manager, Ansarul Haque, for the period he was in charge of Khatunganj Branch.
